procedural_matters: FRA 226430 was represented by Guillermo Dominguez Marvillet.
GBR 228326 was represented by Oliver Mayo.
Johannes Erichsen (regional judge in training) attended the hearing as an observer.
facts: The conditions at the time of theincident were 5 knots of wind and small choppy waves.
FRA 226430 and GBR 228326 were bothsailing downwind on port tack and approching the leeward mark, before thereach to the finish.
When FRA 226430 entered the zone shewas outside overlaped to two unidentified boats and she was clear ahead of GBR 228326.
When FRA 226430 was abeam ofthe mark she slowed down behind the two unidentified boats who were rounding themark.
FRA 226430 luffed closing the gapbetween her and the mark and at the same time GBR 228326 sailed between FRA 226430 and the mark, and established an inside overlap.
The distance between GBR 228326 and the mark was 10 cm.
FRA 226430 luffed and immediately there was contactwith the port side of her bow and GBR 228326's starboard side of the hull, amidships.
There was no damage or injury.
conclusions: GBR 228326 not overlapped with FRA 226430 and not in the zone at the time FRA 226430 reached the zone, failed to give FRA 226430 mark-room, and broke RRS 18.2(a)(2).
GBR 228326 to windward failed to keep clear of FRA 226430 to leeward and broke RRS 11.
GBR 228326 did not avoid contact with FRA 226430 even though it was reasonably possible, and broke RRS 14(a).

When it became clear that GBR 228326 was not keeping clear and giving mark-room it was reasonably possible for FRA 226430, the right-of-way boat and the boat sailing within the mark-room to which she was entitled to avoid contact with GBR 228326. FRA 226430 broke RRS 14(a).
Since FRA 226430 was right-of-way boat and sailing within the mark-room to which she was entitled and the contact did not cause damage or injury she is exonerated for RRS 14(a) under RRS 43.1(c).
